>

> apples and oranges.

> number of people. It'll probably also incur the most
> interaction with users longer term.

>
> Fixing up the existing functions and making them more robust
> and faster will, well, make Stan go faster.
>
> - Bob

messages.subject: PyStan
parts:
I'd first get in contact with Rob to see what he's
managed to do --- maybe you could start where he left
off.

Otherwise, there are several options for wrapping
C++, but I don't know the pros and cons.

As a model of what you want to do, there's RStan.
We pretty much just want to build RStan in Python.
Ideally with as few other dependencies as possible.
You'll probably need to use numpy.

This should all be done vs. Stan 2.0 at this point.
My number one priority now is to review the new command
structure and work on outstanding bug issues.

- Bob

messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] PyStan
parts:
Hi,

re: pystan

I'm trying to mirror the api I find in the rstan-dev github repo right now. Are
there significant changes to the RStan api in the works?

My strategy is to have something api compatible with RStan with the following
deviations:

- obvious pythonic replacements: fit.extract(...) instead of extract(fit, ...)
- less obvious pythonic replacements; dictionaries (OrderedDict) instead of
R lists, numpy arrays instead of R matrices.
- No attempt to allow variables to be referenced by string (e.g. specifying
model_code or data with a string naming a variable). Python is
pass-by-reference so there's no need..

I've still got to figure out the install-time compilation of libstan.a and
libstanc.a and the run-time compilation of models. The hard work (wrapping cpp
with Cython) is finished.

I should have something tomorrow, I think. I'll post a link to the github repo.

Best,

Allen

p.s. I'm targeting Python 3.3, Cython 19.1. I don't think backporting to Python
2.7 should be too difficult.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] PyStan
parts:
>> - obvious pythonic replacements: fit.extract(...) instead of
>> extract(fit, ...)
>> - less obvious pythonic replacements; dictionaries (OrderedDict) instead of
>> R lists, numpy arrays instead of R matrices.

Makes sense. I think ordered dictionaries should be
just like lists if they nest.

>> - No attempt to allow variables to be referenced by string (e.g. specifying
>> model_code or data with a string naming a variable). Python is
>> pass-by-reference so there's no need..

We need something like name=value so we know which values
correspond to which variables. Having the strings just avoided
the R idiom of list(a=a,b=b,...), where the LHS a is a variable
name and the RHS is the value. But just having c(a,b,c), the
array of values, wouldn't be enough because you wouldn't know what the values
referred to.

- Bob
